title: AI Fluency for Small Businesses
author: Anthropic + PayPal
summary: A 9-lesson course, taught by real small-business owners, on choosing which tasks to hand to AI, handling customer data responsibly, and writing an AI use policy, built on the 4D framework.
who_for: Founders and staff new to AI who want a structured, vetted foundation before subscribing to or rolling out Claude.
skip_if: You are already AI-fluent and want product mechanics rather than a decision framework.
notes: Official and free; certificate on completion. Examples use Claude.ai but any chatbot works. No upsell.

title: AI Fluency: Framework & Foundations
author: Anthropic / Profs. Rick Dakan & Joseph Feller
summary: The foundational course teaching the 4D framework (Delegation, Description, Discernment, Diligence) for effective, ethical, and safe AI collaboration.
who_for: Anyone who wants the conceptual backbone before diving into product-specific workflows.
skip_if: You only want quick, copy-paste task recipes.
notes: Prerequisite for the SMB and nonprofit variants. Certificate on completion.

title: Claude 101
author: Anthropic
summary: The shortest official on-ramp: core chat, Projects, files, and connectors for everyday work.
who_for: People who have never opened Claude and want the basics fast.
skip_if: You have used Claude regularly for months.
notes: Free; no coding. Also mirrored on DataCamp and Coursera.

title: Introduction to Claude Cowork
author: Anthropic
summary: Hands-on course covering the Cowork task loop, plugins and skills, file/research workflows, and steering multi-step work.
who_for: Owners and ops people who want Claude to do real multi-step work, not just chat.
skip_if: You have no paid plan to practice on (Cowork needs Pro/Max/Team).
notes: The single most relevant course for running a business. Free course; requires a paid plan to actually practice.

title: Using Claude Cowork for your small business
author: Anthropic
summary: Walks four real workflows step-by-step: plan payroll, close the month, get a Monday brief, and run a campaign.
who_for: Owners who have installed the plugin and want concrete first workflows.
skip_if: You have not installed the plugin yet (read the install guide first).
notes: Official; honest about approval gates and permission inheritance. No upsell.

title: How to install and use the Claude for Small Business plugin
author: Anthropic
summary: The exact click-path to install the plugin, connect tools (QuickBooks, PayPal, HubSpot and more), and customize skills to your business.
who_for: Anyone setting up the plugin for the first time.
skip_if: You are not on the desktop app with a Pro/Max/Team plan.
notes: Explains that connectors inherit each user's existing permissions.

title: Small Business plugin (skill inventory)
author: Anthropic
summary: The authoritative inventory of 15 commands and 15 building-block skills (cash-flow forecasting, invoice chasing, lead triage, contract review, tax prep, hiring packet) and the connectors they use.
who_for: Owners deciding which workflows are worth turning on first.
skip_if: You want a tutorial rather than a catalog.
notes: Lists /plan-payroll, /close-month, /run-campaign, /monday-brief. Notes workflows 'degrade gracefully' when a connector is missing.

title: knowledge-work-plugins/small-business (source repo)
author: Anthropic
summary: The open-source definitions of every SMB skill and command, so you can read and modify exactly what each one does.
who_for: More technical owners or consultants who want to customize or audit the skills.
skip_if: You don't want to look under the hood.
notes: Official Anthropic repo. Install via claude.com/plugins.

title: Introducing Claude for Small Business (launch post)
author: Anthropic
summary: The primary announcement: what the package is, the 8 connectors, the 15 workflows/skills, and the free training and tour.
who_for: Anyone wanting the authoritative overview and the 'you approve before it sends, posts, or pays' safety model.
skip_if: You already understand the offering.
notes: Primary source; states Anthropic does not train on business data on Team/Enterprise by default.

title: How people are using Claude Cowork (usage data)
author: Anthropic
summary: Anthropic's own data showing business-process/operations is the #1 Cowork use at 33.4% of 1.2 million sampled sessions, ahead of content creation (16.4%) and coding (8.7%).
who_for: Owners calibrating realistic expectations of what Cowork is actually good for.
skip_if: You just want how-to steps.
notes: Data sampled May 11–31, 2026 across 600,000+ organizations.

title: Get started with Claude Cowork (Help Center)
author: Anthropic
summary: Canonical reference for permission modes, scheduled tasks, projects, browser actions, and current limits.
who_for: Anyone who wants the definitive, always-current feature reference.
skip_if: You want guided workflows, not reference material.
notes: Kept current as Cowork changes; covers what Cowork cannot do.

title: Plans & Pricing
author: Anthropic
summary: The live, authoritative price/seat/usage-limit table for Free, Pro, Max, Team, and Enterprise.
who_for: Anyone comparing plans before buying.
skip_if: N/A — always verify pricing here rather than in third-party posts.
notes: The only source that won't drift; Anthropic notes prices are subject to change.

title: What is the Team plan? (Help Center)
author: Anthropic
summary: What Team Standard and Premium seats include versus Pro, plus usage credits and centralized admin/billing.
who_for: Owners deciding whether a team of 5+ should move from Pro to Team.
skip_if: You're a solo user — Pro is fine.
notes: Pairs with the pricing page. Team has a 5-seat minimum; usage limits are per-member, not pooled.

title: Is my data used for model training? (Privacy Center)
author: Anthropic
summary: The authoritative statement of what is and isn't used for training, including that raw connector data (e.g., Google Drive, MCP servers) is excluded.
who_for: Anyone worried about data privacy — the #1 SMB hesitation.
skip_if: N/A.
notes: On consumer plans you must toggle 'Help Improve Claude' off; commercial plans exclude training by default.

title: Claude Team pricing for a small business
author: SSD Nodes
summary: Seat math for 3–15 person teams, when an API key beats a seat, and worked examples at 5 and 12 people.
who_for: Owners doing the buy-vs-not math for a small team.
skip_if: You prefer the official pricing page (this adds interpretation, not authority).
notes: Contains an affiliate-style 15%-off code (LEARN15) — ignore it; verify all numbers against claude.com/pricing.

title: How To Use Claude Cowork To Run Your Business With AI
author: Forbes / Jodie Cook (featuring Allie K. Miller)
summary: A founder-level walkthrough of Cowork with honest caveats, including that the 'last mile' of a task can take as long as the first half.
who_for: Founders wanting a credible, no-hype overview from a named expert.
skip_if: A Forbes paywall blocks you.
notes: No income promises; realistic about limits. Written before Cowork went GA, so some access details are dated.

title: Claude Cowork in 5 Minutes
author: Allie K. Miller
summary: A non-technical quick-start guide from first task to scheduled workflows that run on autopilot.
who_for: Busy owners who want to be productive in Cowork in one sitting.
skip_if: You want depth rather than a fast start.
notes: From a genuine Fortune-500 AI advisor; email opt-in for the guide but no paid course funnel.

title: Claude for Small Business setup (decision tree + 15 workflows)
author: WotAI
summary: A decision tree for whether to install the plugin, an honest comparison to ChatGPT Team, and a note that the plugin adds nothing to your bill.
who_for: Owners weighing whether the plugin is worth setting up.
skip_if: You want official steps — use Anthropic's tutorials.
notes: Balanced; explicitly names when to skip it (browser-only teams, Linux, <3 integrations).

title: Claude for Small Business plugin: 31 skills that run your operations
author: Wright Mode
summary: Explains the skills-vs-plugins distinction, the customization step most people skip, and how to remap US-centric defaults to your country.
who_for: Non-US owners and anyone who found the plugin 'too generic' before customizing it.
skip_if: You only need the official install steps.
notes: Honest about US/QuickBooks defaults; no income claims.

title: AI for Small Business: Getting Started with Claude (SBA event)
author: U.S. Small Business Administration
summary: A live introductory webinar on navigating Claude's interface, writing effective prompts, uploading your own business documents, and building a repeatable process.
who_for: Owners who prefer a live, vendor-neutral government session.
skip_if: The listed date has passed — check sba.gov for the next scheduled session.
notes: One-off event listing, not evergreen content; SBA district offices run these recurringly with no upsell.

title: A Comprehensive Guide to AI Training for Small Businesses
author: US Chamber of Commerce (CO—)
summary: A regularly-updated directory of free and low-cost AI courses, books, and tools for small businesses, including resources that cover Claude.
who_for: Owners who want a trustworthy, curated map of options.
skip_if: You want to learn Claude directly rather than browse a list.
notes: One SCORE link in this guide is stale (see Dead links); otherwise a reputable aggregator.

title: AI for Small Business: Explore Tools and Build Systems
author: SCORE (SBA resource partner)
summary: A self-paced course that helps owners spot automatable admin time-drains and compare AI tools including Claude, ChatGPT, NotebookLM, and Perplexity.
who_for: Owners wanting a vendor-neutral, SBA-backed intro to choosing AI tools.
skip_if: You only want Claude context — stop after the free Part 1; Part 2 (the 'AI Business Manifesto') is a $99 upgrade.
notes: Only Part 1 is free; the 'free course' framing in third-party write-ups overstates what's included. Instructor: Robyn Anderson.

title: AI Fluency for Nonprofits
author: Anthropic + GivingTuesday
summary: The 4D framework adapted for mission-driven work: research, grant proposals, donor communications, and program data analysis.
who_for: Nonprofit staff across fundraising, communications, program delivery, operations, and leadership.
skip_if: You run a for-profit business — use the small-business version.
notes: Free; certificate on completion. Nonprofits also qualify for up to 75% off Team/Enterprise plans.

title: Introduction to Model Context Protocol
author: Anthropic
summary: Teaches you to build MCP servers and clients from scratch in Python to connect Claude to external tools and data.
who_for: Technical owners, consultants, or in-house devs who need custom integrations beyond the built-in connectors.
skip_if: You're non-technical — use the one-click built-in connectors instead.
notes: Official, from the team that created MCP. Requires Python/CLI comfort.

title: Remote MCP Servers directory
author: mcpservers.org
summary: A curated list of official one-click remote MCP servers (HubSpot, Stripe, Notion, Linear, Mercury, Attio, and more) that work with Claude.
who_for: Owners/consultants connecting Claude to business tools beyond the built-in SMB connectors.
skip_if: The built-in SMB connectors already cover your stack.
notes: Curated to official/first-party servers, which are the lower-security-risk choice.

title: awesome-mcp-enterprise
author: bh-rat (community)
summary: A curated list of enterprise-grade MCP tools, including unified handlers that connect to hundreds of CRM/accounting/HRIS tools (Merge, Pipedream) and security/governance layers.
who_for: Teams that need governed, security-reviewed integrations.
skip_if: You want simple consumer one-click tools.
notes: Community-maintained; filters for governance/security rather than popularity.

title: Claude for Small Business (Back-Office AI, honest review)
author: Eigent AI
summary: A review that spells out who the plugin is for and who should skip it (regulated shops, no-AI-on-customer-data policies, Microsoft-only teams, owners uncomfortable approving AI actions).
who_for: Owners deciding whether the plugin fits their business and risk profile.
skip_if: You've already decided to adopt it.
notes: Vendor blog but even-handed; explicit 'skip if' list. Verify pricing against claude.com/pricing.
